messages:
maria_devex: Heads up — a few new users hit a crash in the JS SDK sample when deploying to Vercel Edge today. Looks like it started after the recent package `exports` change. Repro + logs below — anyone seen this before? :thinking:

jonathan: error logs? stack? quick repro steps?

maria_devex: Repro steps (minimal):
1) `npx create-redwood-sample && cd sample-app`
2) `npm i redwood-sdk@^2.6.0` (we have a pinned sample to 2.6.0)
3) deploy to edge (Vercel Edge Runtime)

Error shown on the edge function: `TypeError: default is not a constructor` and in runtime console: `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'create')`

Also TypeScript in the sample shows: `TS1192: Module '"redwood-sdk"' has no default export.`

Here's the import in the sample:```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.KEY });
```

jonathan: Hmm. Sounds like an ESM/CJS interop issue — maybe the export map now points the main entry at a CJS bundle but the edge runtime prefers ESM. Did the recent change add a conditional field for `node`/`default`?

samir: Yep — I shipped the export map tweak last week to improve node resolution for some internal tools. The change added an explicit `require` path and a `node` conditional to keep older Node versions happy. Problem is the edge/platform resolves the package to the CJS entry and then TS/ESM imports fail. Oops.

maria_devex: For surface-level workaround I told a user to change the import to `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` which works, or to pin to 2.5.x. But that defeats onboarding.

tasha: Is there a quick patch we can publish? A rollback of the export map would be safest. Also the samples use `type: module` so they expect proper ESM semantics.

samir: I'm putting together a patch PR to restore an explicit ESM path and add an `edge` conditional in the `exports` so edge runtime gets `./dist/esm/index.js` and Node 12/14 still get the fallback. Opening PR now: redwood-inference/sdk#4212.

cli-bot: CI report — sample-app-integration (canary) failed on deploy: https://ci/internal/7890 — 3 instances crashed with the same runtime error.

alex_ml: Also seeing type regression in the SDK types: `index.d.ts` wasn't exported through the `types` conditional, so `npm pack` + external bundlers fell back to no types. That explains TS complaints in the sample.

samir: Good catch. I'll add "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" to the package manifest inside the PR and ensure `exports` includes "types" mapping for TS-aware resolvers.

jonathan: Can we also add a CI job that validates our package `exports` across targets (node12/node16/edge/tsc) so this doesn't slip by again? A quick matrix test would catch this.

maria_devex: Yes please — onboarding gets blocked if samples break on first run. I'll add a note in the onboarding doc to pin to `2.6.0` with a short explanation until the patch lands.

samir: Plan: revert the problematic export map change in `2.6.1-patch`, publish a `2.6.2` that contains the ESM-first export map + proper `types` mapping, and add the CI matrix job. Target timeline: revert PR out in ~30m, publish patch in next hour if green.

tasha: I'll queue a canary deploy of the sample app against the patch once it's published.

maria_devex: Thanks — I'll update the quickstart doc and send a small customer-facing note to the onboarding slack channel if the patch goes out. :pray:

samir: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4212 (WIP) — adding tests and types mapping now.

jonathan: After this, let's add a tiny e2e that runs `npm pack` and installs the tarball in a minimal `type: module` app to validate runtime + types. Recommending we make that part of release gating.

maria_devex: perfect. keeping users posted.

alex_ml: fyi I found one user who avoided the break by importing directly from `redwood-sdk/dist/esm/index.js` — that's OK as a short-term note but not ideal for onboarding.

samir: Agreed. I'll revert and push patch now.

maria_devex: I'll update the sample PR to point at the patched version when it's published and remove the pin once verified.

jonathan: thanks team. quick and clean fix will save a lot of tickets.
